porbos.title: The First Revelation • The Burden That Can Be Lifted by One Sentence • The Proof That Stood Before the Claim

blocks.1: As he approached forty, a restlessness was gathering inside him. Idols all around, the killing of daughters, the tyranny over the weak; no one had any answer to these.
blocks.2: He began to stay alone. A little way from Makkah, near the top of Jabal al-Nur, there is a small cave; its name is Hira. Taking food he would go there and stay for days on end, especially staying longer in the month of Ramadan. When the food ran out he would return to Makkah and take more. The name of this seclusion is tahannuth; worship, reflection, searching for Allah in solitude.
blocks.4: He is sitting in the cave of Hira.
blocks.5: Age forty. The month of Ramadan. Deep night.
blocks.6: Suddenly he sensed a presence. In the dark cave he was no longer alone.
blocks.7: An angel. His name Jibril (AS). In his hand something wrapped in cloth.
blocks.9: The Prophet {{1}} said, I do not know how to read. Jibril embraced him, pressed him with all his strength; so hard that his breath was almost stopped. Then he let go and said again, Iqra.
blocks.10: The same reply. The same pressure. It happened three times.{{1}}
blocks.11: The third time, letting go, Jibril said
blocks.13: Read in the name of your Lord who created. Created man from a clot of blood. Read, and your Lord is the Most Generous. Who taught by the pen. Taught man what he did not know.{{1}}
blocks.14: Five verses. The first revelation. In the darkness of the cave that day prophethood came down.
blocks.15: Jibril vanished. The Prophet {{1}} came out of the cave trembling. His heart pounding. Returning home he said, cover me, cover me.
blocks.16: Khadijah (RA) wrapped a cloth around him. She sat beside him. When the fear eased a little he told her everything.
blocks.17: He said, I fear for myself.
blocks.18: Khadijah did not hesitate even a moment. She said, no. By Allah, Allah will never disgrace you. You uphold the ties of kinship, you carry the burden of the weak, you give to the penniless, you honour the guest, and on days of calamity you stand by the truth.{{1}}
blocks.19: A man is trembling with fear; and to give him courage no argument is needed, what is needed is his forty years of life. Character became his greatest reassurance that day.
blocks.20: Khadijah took him to her cousin Waraqah ibn Nawfal. An old, blind Christian scholar; who had the Torah and Injil by heart.
blocks.21: The Prophet {{1}} told the whole event in his own words.
blocks.22: Waraqah listened. Then he said, this is the same Namus that Allah sent to Musa (AS). He said, oh, if only I were young then! Oh, if only I were alive on the day your people drive you out!
blocks.23: The Prophet {{1}} asked in astonishment, will they drive me out?
blocks.24: Waraqah said, yes. Whoever has come with anything like what you have come with has been met with hostility. And if I live to see that day, I will help you with all my strength.{{1}}
blocks.25: Not long after saying these words Waraqah passed away. He could not live to see that prediction come true with his own eyes.
blocks.26: Fatrat al-Wahy, the Pause of Revelation
blocks.27: After this revelation paused for some time. This period is named Fatrat al-Wahy. In the heart of the Prophet {{1}} there was then an unrest. Will revelation not come again?
blocks.28: One day he was walking. Suddenly he heard a voice from the sky. He lifted his eyes and looked. He saw the same angel who had come in Hira; Jibril (AS). Seated on a throne between the sky and the earth.{{1}}
blocks.29: Trembling with fear he returned home. He said, cover me, cover me.
blocks.32: O you wrapped in your cloak! Arise and warn. And your Lord, magnify. And your garments, purify. And uncleanness, avoid.{{1}}
blocks.33: From here revelation began again; this time it did not stop, it kept coming one after another.
blocks.34: What command was given? In the first revelation it was said, read. And in this second revelation came, arise, warn. A man was first told to read himself, then told to inform others. Before beginning the work of da‘wah, one’s own preparation; this is the order.
blocks.36: How this revelation actually descended, that question was once put directly to the Prophet {{1}}. Harith ibn Hisham asked, O Messenger of Allah {{2}}! How does revelation come to you? The Prophet {{3}} said, sometimes it comes like the sound of a bell; this is its heaviest form, when revelation ends I have grasped what was said. And sometimes the angel takes the form of a man, comes before me and speaks; his words I grasp directly.{{4}}
blocks.37: ‘A’ishah (RA) says, even on a bitterly cold day, when revelation came down upon him, sweat poured down his forehead; so heavy was every moment.
blocks.38: In one moment three kinds of testimony stood together. The angel had come straight from the sky. The wife had stood, relying on the character known for forty years. And an old scholar had matched it with the earlier Book.
blocks.39: From here began that claim of prophethood, whose proof we will now set out to look for.
blocks.40: The Burden That Can Be Lifted by One Sentence
blocks.41: What did Khadijah (RA) do that day!
blocks.42: Her husband came into the house trembling. He said, cover me with a cloak. Then what he said had nothing but terror in it; I fear for my own life.
blocks.43: What would we have done! We would have asked questions. What happened, where did you go, who was with you. Or we would have given advice. What is there to be so afraid of, be patient. Or made light of it. Nothing happened, you are overthinking.
blocks.44: She did none of these. She did not ask questions. She did not give advice. She said, never; Allah will never disgrace you.
blocks.45: And what she did after that is the real point. She gave reasons. You uphold the ties of kinship. You carry the burden of the helpless. You earn for the penniless. You serve the guest. You help the one in distress.{{1}}
blocks.46: She did not want to chase the fear away. She showed her husband his own life. She said, the man who has lived this way, Allah will not abandon him. The consolation did not come from the sky; it came from the account of real life.
blocks.47: Now come into today’s home. The boy has come home having done badly in the exam. The girl has come back weeping from her in-laws’ house. The husband’s job is gone.
blocks.48: What do we say! I told you earlier. Now you see! How many times must I tell you! The words may be true. But before a broken person even a true word falls like a stone.
blocks.49: A broken person does not want advice. He wants a person who will say; I know you, and you are not like this.
blocks.50: In the heaviest moment of bearing the burden of prophethood, the one who stood beside the Prophet {{1}} was no scholar. She was his wife. And what she gave was not knowledge; it was testimony.
blocks.51: So take one task from today’s lesson. Find the person in your home who is broken right now. Do not give advice. Remind him of one of the good deeds of his life. The burden will come down right there.
blocks.52: The Proof That Stood Before the Claim
blocks.53: At forty a man stood up and said, I am the Messenger of Allah. Naturally the question arises, what is the proof? Anyone can make a claim.
blocks.55: Now come to the market of Makkah. A man is going to a far land. He must leave behind his saved gold and silver. With whom will he leave it? The city has no lack of famous men. There are tribal chiefs, rich merchants, old respected elders. Yet people’s feet move toward one particular house. The house of Muhammad, son of ‘Abdullah.
blocks.56: The whole city knows him by one name. Al-Amin. The trustworthy. No party gave him this name. No announcement set it going. It settled by itself on people’s lips. And the greatest point is this; those who would later become his bitterest enemies, who would want to shed his blood, when it came to leaving a trust they too came to this very house.
blocks.57: The Trust on the Night of the Hijrah
blocks.58: The night of the Hijrah. The enemies surround the house with swords in hand. And that very night he is leaving ‘Ali (RA) behind, so that the trusts people had deposited could be returned.{{1}}
blocks.59: The trusts of those who had come to kill him. The enmity so deep; yet the trust had not shifted in the least.
blocks.60: The calculation is this. At forty he claimed prophethood. But the proof of his honesty had been standing forty years before that. In the enemy’s own hand. In the enemy’s own testimony. This is the first evidence of prophethood. No sky split. No mountain moved. Only one man’s character bore witness for forty years. A man who has not told one lie in forty years, that he would suddenly one day tell the greatest lie in Allah’s name; by what reasoning could that be accepted!
blocks.62: A scene from a few years later.
blocks.63: One thing I say at the outset. This incident is much later. Six or seven years after the Hijrah; during the time of the treaty of Hudaybiyyah, when the Prophet {{1}} sent letters to various royal courts. Then why bring it here? Because today’s discussion is not the order of time; it is the order of proof. And this is a proof that did not come from the mouth of any Muslim. It came from the mouth of an enemy, standing in the enemy’s own court.
blocks.64: In a city of Syria, the court of the Roman emperor Heraclius. A golden throne, courtiers standing in rows all around. News comes that an Arab merchant caravan from Makkah has come on business. The emperor ordered, bring the leader of the caravan into court.
blocks.65: The one who was brought was named Abu Sufyan. At that time one of the Prophet’s {{1}} greatest enemies. With his own hand he had taken up the sword and fought against him. Today he stands in an unfamiliar royal court, among people of an unfamiliar language, alone.
blocks.66: The interpreter stood beside. The emperor said, I will ask you some questions about this man. Your companions are standing behind you; if you lie, they will catch you out before me. So tell the truth.
blocks.67: Abu Sufyan later told this incident himself. He said, by Allah, if that day there had not been the fear that my own people would call me a liar, I would have lied about him without worry. That very fear that day stood a fierce enemy on the side of truth.
blocks.68: The questions began, one after another. How is his lineage? Of high lineage. Did any of his forefathers claim kingship earlier? No. Before his claim of prophethood, was he ever suspected of lying? No, never. Are his followers increasing or decreasing? Increasing, day by day. Having entered his religion, does anyone leave displeased? Never. Does he ever break a pledge? No.{{1}}
blocks.69: After each question a small silence; Abu Sufyan thinking what to say. Each time the truth came out of his mouth, and each time that truth went and stood on the side of his own enemy.
blocks.70: At the end of all the questions Heraclius was silent for a while. Then he said slowly, if all you have said is true, this man will very soon take even the ground beneath these two feet of mine.
blocks.71: The court was still. A Roman emperor, seated on his own throne, drew out the proof of prophethood from the mouth of a polytheist leader of Makkah; and that polytheist leader had not yet accepted Islam.
blocks.73: The proof was a man’s character.
blocks.74: The man who was still fighting against him, standing before the emperor, that very man ended up telling the truth.
blocks.75: In our case the calculation sticks exactly here.
blocks.76: People read us before they listen to us.
blocks.77: What the scales in the shop are like, whether words are broken, what comes out of the mouth in anger.
blocks.78: After all that has been read, we begin to speak of the religion.
blocks.79: Then the words no longer carry weight.

quiz.q: In the first revelation, how many times did Jibril (AS) press the Prophet ﷺ and say ‘Iqra’?
o: Three times, each time the Prophet ﷺ said I do not know how to read
Twice, the verses were revealed the second time
Once, then the verses began to be revealed
Four times, the verses were revealed at the fourth, as is generally held
quiz.e: After each ‘Iqra’ the Prophet ﷺ said I do not know how to read, and Jibril pressed him again; only after this happened three times were the verses of Surah al-‘Alaq revealed (Sahih al-Bukhari hadith 3).

quiz.q: When Khadijah (RA) consoled the Prophet ﷺ, what did she chiefly bring up?
o: The honour of his lineage and tribal standing, as is generally held
His long-proven honesty and good character
His business skill and profit
His eloquence and skill in speech
quiz.e: Khadijah brought up not arguments but the Prophet’s ﷺ long-proven character; upholding kinship, carrying the burden of the weak, giving to the penniless, hospitality and standing by the truth; mentioning these qualities she explained that Allah would never disgrace him.

quiz.q: After Fatrat al-Wahy, how did revelation come the second time?
o: Going back to the cave of Hira in the same manner again
Hearing Jibril’s voice inside a dream
Seeing Jibril seated on a throne between the sky and the earth
Suddenly hearing a sound in Khadijah’s house
quiz.e: After being frightened at seeing Jibril seated on a throne between the sky and the earth and returning, the first verses of Surah al-Muddaththir were revealed, in which the command was, arise, warn.

quiz.q: How many kinds of testimony stood together around the first revelation?
o: Two kinds
Four kinds
Three kinds
No testimony stood at all
quiz.e: The testimony of the angel (from the sky), the testimony of the wife (the character of forty years) and the testimony of Waraqah (agreement with the earlier Book); that these three kinds came one after another and matched is no coincidence.

quiz.q: From the order of the commands of the first revelation (read) and the second (arise, warn), what can be learned about the work of da‘wah?
o: Informing others comes first, one’s own preparation later
There is no order between the two commands
Only after one’s own preparation should others be informed
The first command alone was enough for da‘wah
quiz.e: First read (knowing oneself), then arise and warn (informing others); this order points to the right method of da‘wah.

quiz.q: Someone said, looking for argument behind a religious claim means weaker faith. What reply comes from this lesson?
o: No, even ‘Abdullah ibn Salam believed only after verifying by questions
This is really an irrelevant question here
Yes, asking is wrong, one should accept with eyes closed, as is generally held
Looking for argument applies only to non-Muslims
quiz.e: ‘Abdullah ibn Salam, understanding in his heart from the face, still verified by asking three hard questions; Heraclius too reached the truth by asking question after question. Verifying by argument and faith are not opposed.

quiz.q: In standing by someone in family or at work, relying only on his character without giving arguments; how reasonable can this be?
o: A proven character can be a strong foundation
Character has no value in making decisions
It is unreasonable, specific arguments are always needed, as is generally held
One should trust only new acquaintances
quiz.e: Khadijah (RA) consoled him without argument, relying on the Prophet’s ﷺ long-proven character; in close relationships this is sometimes the greatest strength.

quiz.q: Among the qualities of her husband that Khadijah (RA) mentioned in consoling him was
o: He does much worship and keeps vigil at night
He is the greatest merchant and a man of wealth, as is generally held
He upholds the ties of kinship, carries the burden of the helpless
He is the child of the most honoured lineage of the Quraysh
quiz.e: Hadith 3 of Sahih al-Bukhari; along with it were earning for the penniless, serving the guest and helping the one in distress.

quiz.q: How was Khadijah’s (RA) manner of consoling different from others’?
o: She advised taking him to Waraqah, as is generally held
Instead of chasing away the fear, she showed her husband his own life
She wanted to learn the details of the incident
She wanted to make light of the matter
quiz.e: The consolation did not come from the sky; it came from the account of real life.

quiz.q: When someone in the family is broken, what is the most effective act according to this lesson?
o: To remind him of one of the good deeds of his life
To advise patience
To learn in detail what happened
To make light of it by not giving it importance
quiz.e: A broken person does not want advice; he wants a person who will say, I know you, and you are not like this.

quiz.q: On the night of the Hijrah, though the enemies had surrounded the house, why did the Prophet ﷺ leave ‘Ali (RA) there?
o: To guard the entrance of the house
To hold a last discussion with the enemies, as is generally held
To protect Khadijah’s wealth
To return the trusts people had deposited
quiz.e: Even under the threat of death he did not drop returning people’s trusts; the trusts of those who had come to kill him were deposited in that very house too.

quiz.q: What was the main purpose of the questions the Roman emperor Heraclius asked Abu Sufyan?
o: To match lineage and character with the traits of a prophet
To humiliate Abu Sufyan in court
To gather secret information about Makkah’s military strength
To learn the accounts of the Arab merchants’ trade
quiz.e: Lineage, forefathers’ claim to kingship, earlier honesty, increase of followers, keeping pledges; every question was a measure for verifying the traits of a true prophet.

quiz.q: How can the main argument of the section ‘The Proof That Stood Before the Claim’ be applied in the case of any other person?
o: Past conduct is entirely irrelevant to decisions
Anyone’s claim should always be believed without question, as is generally held
One should judge only by outward appearance
One should verify truthfulness by looking at the history of a person’s past conduct
quiz.e: After forty years of proven honesty, the possibility of suddenly lying is not reasonable; this principle is useful in verifying anyone’s trustworthiness.

quiz.q: Why is the conversation of Heraclius and Abu Sufyan especially important as testimony?
o: Because Abu Sufyan later forgot his words, as is generally held
Because the testimony came from the mouth of the Prophet’s ﷺ bitterest enemy
Because Heraclius himself was a Muslim
Because the incident was written many years later
quiz.e: The involuntary testimony of an enemy is worth more than the testimony of a neutral person or a friend; Abu Sufyan had no interest in telling the truth; rather, fear of shame compelled him.

quiz.q: If you know someone’s long-standing honesty but suddenly hear an unusual claim from him, what, according to the lesson’s principle, is the first thing to do?
o: Only to follow the opinion of the majority
To disbelieve the claim at once
To verify it, keeping the earlier proven character in view
To avoid the matter without deciding, as is generally held
quiz.e: Long-proven honesty adds extra credibility behind a person’s words; yet the way of verification remains open, not blind belief.

quiz.q: If you feel discouraged because others do not believe your word, which lesson from the character of al-Amin helps?
o: One may resort to falsehood to gain influence, it is held
Long-standing honesty in the end compels people to believe
People never change, and trying is pointless
If there are no immediate results, honesty should be abandoned
quiz.e: It was forty years of honesty that gave the Prophet ﷺ the title al-Amin, not a single day; keeping honesty with patience is what builds credibility in the long run.

porbos.title: The Miracle That Still Lies Open • The Moon Split in Two

blocks.0: The Miracle That Still Lies Open
blocks.1: Allah gave every prophet a miracle. But He gave it by measure; suited to the age.
blocks.2: In the age of Musa (AS) sorcery was flourishing. So the staff in his hand became a snake. And the first to fall down in prostration were the sorcerers themselves. Because they understood better than anyone that this was not sorcery.{{1}}
blocks.3: In the age of ‘Isa (AS) medicine was triumphant. So at his hand blind eyes opened, and the dead stood up.{{1}}
blocks.4: And in the age of the Prophet {{1}}! Arabia had only one thing to be proud of. Language. In the grounds of ‘Ukaz the gatherings of the poets were held. Whoever's poem was the best, it was written in gold and hung on the wall of the Ka‘bah. Before that very people Allah placed a miracle of language itself.
blocks.6: Then He threw down the challenge. The first challenge was of the largest scale; bring something like the whole Qur’an.
blocks.8: Say, even if mankind and the jinn were to gather together to bring something equal to this Qur’an, they would still not be able to bring anything equal to it; even if they were helpers to one another.{{1}}
blocks.9: When even humans and jinn all together achieved nothing, Allah reduced the limit; not the whole Qur’an, bring just ten surahs like it.
blocks.11: Or do they say, he has invented it himself? Say, then bring ten invented surahs like it; and call upon whomever you can besides Allah, if you are truthful.{{1}}
blocks.12: Even then no one came forward. At last the limit came down to the very bottom; just one surah.
blocks.14: And if you are in doubt about what I have sent down upon My servant, then bring one surah like it; and call upon your helpers besides Allah, if you are truthful.{{1}}
blocks.15: One surah. Just one. For people who had dealt in words all their lives, this is nothing at all. Yet no one could. The challenge kept shrinking from the biggest to the smallest, until it came to rest at the easiest place; still no one could touch it.
blocks.16: The Testimony of al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah
blocks.17: In the assembly of Quraysh there was an unease at that time. The Hajj season was coming. People would come from outside, and after hearing the Qur’an from the mouth of the Prophet {{1}} they would go back with hearts changed; out of this fear Quraysh could not sleep.
blocks.18: The leaders rushed to an old man. His name was al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah. The greatest judge of poetry in Arabia; nearly eighty years old. A lifetime of listening to poetry had made his ear so seasoned that on hearing a single line he could say which was the work of a true poet and which a forgery stitched together.
blocks.19: They said, the Hajj season is coming, people accept your word. Give a verdict: is this poetry, or sorcery, or something else.
blocks.20: Walid went. He sat face to face with the Prophet {{1}}. He listened to the Qur’an. As he listened, the lines of his face began to change. With a lifetime's experience he could not place this thing in any familiar category.
blocks.21: He came back. Everyone in the assembly was looking at him; waiting with held breath. He said, by Allah, I have heard a speech that is neither the speech of man nor of the jinn. Its beginning is sweet, its end enchanting. It is above everything; there is nothing above it. And it crushes everything beneath it.{{1}}
blocks.22: The assembly was stunned. This speech had snatched away their very weapon. Abu Jahl rushed to him. Terror on his face. He said, if you go about saying this, your people will think you have entered this religion. Eighty years of honour will be dust in a single day.
blocks.23: Walid sat alone for a while. Head bowed. Forehead creased. Hand on his brow. Once he looked up at the sky, then lowered his eyes again to the ground. On one side a lifetime's honour, on the other the truth he had heard with his own ears. Then he raised his head and said, all right; tell them it is sorcery, learned from before.
blocks.24: The very thing he knew in his heart to be true, that very thing he said with his mouth to be false; only out of fear of becoming small in the eyes of his people, only out of fear of losing the honour earned over eighty years. The Qur’an itself brings out this inner conflict of his,
blocks.26: Indeed, he thought and determined. May he be destroyed, how he determined! Again, may he be destroyed, how he determined! Then he looked. Then he frowned and scowled. Then he turned back and was arrogant. Then he said, this is nothing but sorcery, taught.{{1}}
blocks.27: Acknowledgement in the heart and denial with the mouth; these two can never live in peace inside a person.
blocks.29: Another day another leader of Quraysh, ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah, went himself to the Prophet {{1}}. Taking leave of the assembly he said, let me go and talk; perhaps this time some settlement will come.
blocks.30: He sat face to face. Softening his voice he said, nephew, say what you want. If it is wealth you want, we will all together make you the richest. If it is leadership, we will make you our chief. If it is the most beautiful bride, we will bring her. Only stop this call, stop speaking ill of our gods and goddesses.
blocks.31: The Prophet {{1}} listened silently to all of it. No annoyance on his face. At the end he asked, have you finished? ‘Utbah said, yes.
blocks.32: The Prophet {{1}} said, then listen to me now. And he began reciting from the beginning of Surah Ha-Mim Sajdah.
blocks.33: ‘Utbah put both hands behind his back and leaned on them; in a pose as if listening to an ordinary speech. He listened quietly. Verse after verse. Little by little his leaning body began to straighten. His hands were no longer behind him. When the verses of punishment came, of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of ‘Ad and Thamud; the blood drained from ‘Utbah's face. He stretched out his hand and pressed it over the mouth of the Prophet {{1}}. His voice trembling. He said, stop, stop, for the sake of kinship.{{2}}
blocks.34: Trembling, he returned to the assembly. Face white, eyes blank. Everyone asked, what happened, what have you come back with? ‘Utbah said, by Allah, I have heard a speech such as I have never heard before. It is not poetry, not sorcery, not the utterance of a soothsayer. Listen to me, leave him alone, let him get on with his work.
blocks.35: Quraysh said, ‘Utbah has come back bewitched. But what had happened was not sorcery; it was the trembling of a heart standing before the truth, which even the body could not hide.
blocks.36: The Message from the Mouth of an Unlettered Prophet
blocks.37: There is another thing worth noting. The Prophet {{1}} never studied with any teacher, never learned to write. In the Qur’an itself he is called ummi; unlettered.
blocks.39: And you did not recite any book before it, nor did you write anything with your own hand; in that case the falsifiers would surely have doubted.{{1}}
blocks.40: A man who never sat in any school; from his mouth came the highest literature of the Arabic language, which even great poets could not touch. This one fact alone tells that this message is not his own composition. They raised swords. They arrayed armies. They fought year after year. They forced him out of his home, boycotted him, plotted to kill him. But the one thing that was easiest, writing a single surah and breaking the challenge; that is the one thing no one could do.
blocks.41: Fourteen hundred years have passed. The challenge stands today exactly where it stood. It has not moved an inch.
blocks.42: And here is a great difference. The miracles of the other prophets were seen only by those who saw them with their eyes. No one today can see a staff become a snake. But this miracle lies open before every person of every age. Whoever wishes, let him come and examine it.
blocks.43: The miracle is in our homes too.
blocks.44: On the high shelf of the cupboard, wrapped in cloth.
blocks.45: Taken down once or twice a year. When someone dies, or when Ramadan comes.
blocks.46: We say, if only we saw a sign, our faith would be stronger.
blocks.47: The sign is in the house. It is not opened.
blocks.48: The Book around which the challenge has stood for fourteen hundred years; we do not find the time even to turn one page of it.
blocks.50: A night in the plain of Mina. The sky clear, full of stars; the night calm. The disbelievers of Makkah came and stood there. They said, if you are truly a prophet, show us a sign.
blocks.51: The Prophet {{1}} pointed toward the sky. And the moon split into two pieces. One piece on this side of the mountain, the other on that. Anas, Ibn Mas‘ud and Ibn ‘Abbas (RA); several Companions saw it with their own eyes and bore witness.{{2}}
blocks.52: Now tell me, what is left after this! What did they say!
blocks.54: The Hour has drawn near, and the moon has split. And if they see a sign, they turn away and say, continuous sorcery.{{1}}
blocks.55: The moon split in two. And they said, sorcery.
blocks.56: There is a hard truth here. The problem was not the eyes. There was no shortage of signs. The problem was inside. The door was already shut; so however much light burned outside, not a drop entered. One who wants to keep his eyes shut, even the sun cannot wake him.
blocks.57: More Miracles Seen with the Eyes
blocks.58: The splitting of the moon is not alone.
blocks.59: On the journey of Hudaybiyyah the water ran out. People were restless with thirst. A vessel was brought before the Prophet {{1}}, with a little water in it. He dipped his hand in the vessel. Water began to flow from between his fingers like a spring. The Companions lined up, made ablution and drank; fifteen hundred people, yet the water did not run out.{{2}}
blocks.60: At the time of the Battle of the Trench. Digging the trench, the Companions had put no grain in their stomachs for three days. Jabir (RA) had at home a tiny kid and a little barley; he told his wife, cook, I will invite the Prophet {{1}}. The Prophet {{2}} called the whole army of the Trench and came; about a thousand people. From the small pot and the oven everyone ate their fill, yet the pot stayed full, the bread did not decrease.{{3}}
blocks.61: And the trunk of the date palm against which he used to lean when giving the sermon; after the new wooden pulpit was built, he walked past that old trunk. The mosque full of people heard that the trunk was weeping; a sound like the sobbing of a child. The Prophet {{1}} came down and held the trunk to his chest; then that weeping stopped.{{2}}
blocks.62: Rain over the Sky of Madinah
blocks.63: Once in Madinah there was a severe drought. The fields dried up and cracked, animals were dying, travel on the roads was halted.
blocks.64: The Friday sermon was under way. Suddenly a Bedouin came in through the door and stood straight in front of the pulpit. He said, O Messenger of Allah {{1}}! Our animals are dying, the roads are blocked; pray to Allah for rain.
blocks.65: The Prophet {{1}} raised both hands. He said, O Allah, give us rain, give us rain, give us rain.
blocks.66: Anas (RA) says, by Allah, there was not even a wisp of cloud in the sky then. Between us and Mount Sal‘ there was no house or building that could hide anything. Yet from behind the mountain a cloud rose, small as a shield. Before our eyes it spread to the middle of the sky. Then the rain fell. Anas says, by Allah, after this we did not see the sun for a whole week.{{1}}
blocks.67: The next Friday another man came in through the same door. He said, O Messenger of Allah {{1}}! Houses are collapsing, the roads are blocked; pray to Allah that this rain stops.
blocks.68: The Prophet {{1}} smiled. He said, O Allah, around us, not upon us.
blocks.69: At once the clouds moved away from over Madinah and divided to right and left. Rain began to fall all around the city, not a drop inside the city.{{1}}
blocks.70: Once bringing rain down from the sky, and once turning that rain around the city; both with just a single supplication.
blocks.72: On the eve of the Battle of Khaybar the Prophet {{1}} announced, tomorrow I will give the banner to a man who loves Allah and His Messenger, and at whose hands Allah will grant victory. That night everyone was thinking, in whose hand will the banner fall. As morning came everyone rushed forward; each hoping he would be the one called.
blocks.73: The Prophet {{1}} asked, where is ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib? People said, his eyes are inflamed; he cannot even get up.
blocks.74: He was led in. The Prophet {{1}} applied his own saliva to his eyes and made supplication. In an instant ‘Ali's eyes were healed as if there had never been any pain there.{{2}}
blocks.75: Then he placed the banner in his hand. That very day the fortress of Khaybar was conquered under ‘Ali's leadership.
blocks.77: Even a stone knew him. Even before prophethood a stone in Makkah used to greet him. In his own words he said, I still recognize that stone which used to greet me before prophethood.{{1}}
blocks.79: There is another kind of proof too; not an event seen with the eyes, but a word spoken long before it happened.
blocks.80: At that time there were two superpowers in the world; Persia on one side, Rome on the other. The Persians were worshippers of fire and idols. And the Romans were People of the Book, Christians. At that time Persia was crushing Rome in one war after another. Syria went, Egypt went, even Bayt al-Maqdis fell into Persian hands. The Roman empire was then on the brink of destruction.
blocks.81: When this news reached Makkah the polytheists broke into jubilation. They said, look, idol worshippers have defeated the People of the Book; we will defeat you in the same way. The Muslims were heavy-hearted; for the defeat of the People of the Book seemed a step back for truth itself.
blocks.82: Just at that time was revealed
blocks.84: The Romans have been defeated, in the nearest land; and after their defeat they will soon be victorious, within a few years. The decision belongs to Allah before and after. And on that day the believers will rejoice in the help of Allah; He helps whom He wills, and He is the Almighty, the Most Merciful.{{1}}
blocks.85: In the verse there are two things. One, defeated Rome will win again within a few years. Two, on that very day the believers too will receive joyful news. In Arabic, a few years means between three and nine years.
blocks.86: The polytheists of Makkah heard this prophecy and laughed it off. Ubayy ibn Khalaf made a wager with Abu Bakr (RA); what each would give the other if Rome did not win within so many years was also fixed. The prohibition of gambling had not yet come; that ruling was revealed much later, in Madinah. The Prophet {{1}} later told Abu Bakr, raise the amount of the wager, and make the term longer too.{{2}}
blocks.87: Then what happened matched down to the letter. The Roman emperor Heraclius gathered a huge army and struck back. In a few years the Persian forces were completely defeated. The empire that had been ending just a little earlier rose to its feet again. And at exactly that time, on the plain of Badr, the Muslims gained their first great victory. Both things in the verse came true at about the same time; Rome's victory, and the joy of the believers.{{1}}
blocks.88: A subtle point is also worth noting. The verse says Rome was defeated in the nearest land. The region where that fighting took place, that border of Sham and Palestine, is one of the lowest lands on earth; around the Dead Sea.
blocks.89: A book, writing down the outcome of a war even before the war began; and not one word of that book has changed in fourteen hundred years.
blocks.90: The events are separate. But all together they say one thing; of the one who makes the claim, nature itself is standing as witness in his favour.
blocks.92: Even after seeing the moon split in two, they said, sorcery.
blocks.94: We too say, if we had seen a miracle with our eyes we would have changed.
blocks.95: Those who saw did not change.
blocks.96: What the eye sees, the heart accepts only if it wants to accept.
blocks.97: The problem was not the proof. The problem was the willingness to accept.

quiz.q: Which feature of their respective ages were the miracles of Musa and ‘Isa (AS) matched to?
o: In Musa's age poetry, in ‘Isa's age trade
In Musa's age sorcery, in ‘Isa's age medicine
In both ages architecture was foremost
In Musa's age war, in ‘Isa's age astronomy
quiz.e: Because sorcery flourished in the age of Musa (AS), the miracle of the staff becoming a snake was given; because medicine was triumphant in the age of ‘Isa (AS), the miracle of healing the blind and the dead was given.

quiz.q: In the order of revelation, in what sequence did the challenge to bring something like the Qur’an come?
o: The whole Qur’an, then ten surahs, then one surah
One surah, then ten surahs, then the whole Qur’an
Ten surahs, then one surah, then the whole Qur’an
From beginning to end only the challenge of one surah came
quiz.e: The challenge shrank step by step: first the like of the whole Qur’an (Surah Bani Isra’il 88), then ten surahs (Surah Hud 13), finally just one surah (Surah al-Baqarah 23). The easier the challenge became, the clearer the failure.

quiz.q: What did al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah first acknowledge in his heart on hearing the Qur’an?
o: It is the ordinary utterance of a soothsayer
It is regarded as merely a wonderful poem
It is a copied statement from earlier books
It is not the speech of man or jinn, it is above everything
quiz.e: Walid said, this is neither the speech of man nor of the jinn; its beginning is sweet, its end enchanting, there is nothing above it. Later, under Abu Jahl's pressure, he denied this very same speech by calling it sorcery.

quiz.q: What proposal did ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah make to the Prophet ﷺ?
o: A proposal of temptation by wealth, leadership and marriage
A proposal to stop the fighting directly
A proposal to perform Hajj together
A proposal to leave Makkah, it is regarded
quiz.e: ‘Utbah wanted to stop the call by tempting with wealth, leadership and marriage; when the Prophet ﷺ replied by reciting Surah Ha-Mim Sajdah, hearing the verses of punishment he pressed his hand over the Prophet's ﷺ mouth in fear.

quiz.q: What is the most important difference, mentioned in the lesson, between the miracles of the other prophets and the miracle of the Qur’an?
o: The other miracles were only for that age, the Qur’an is open in every age
The miracles of the other prophets are regarded as comparatively more powerful
The miracle of the Qur’an is impossible to verify
Only Arabic speakers understand the miracle of the Qur’an
quiz.e: No one today can see a staff become a snake, but the linguistic challenge of the Qur’an stands intact even after fourteen hundred years; anyone can verify it even today.

quiz.q: Looking at the incidents of al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah and ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah together, what can be understood about the leaders of Quraysh?
o: Though they felt the truth in their hearts, they denied it openly
They had secretly accepted Islam
They could not understand the language of the Qur’an at all
They genuinely considered the Qur’an false, it is regarded
quiz.e: Both felt the effect of the Qur’an inwardly, but because of social standing and tribal pressure could not acknowledge it openly.

quiz.q: If someone says, it is hard to believe without proof in today's age, what answer does this lesson give?
o: Only the words of the scholars must be accepted without question
The linguistic challenge of the Qur’an is intact even today, one can verify it oneself
Asking for proof is forbidden in the eyes of religion
Belief has no need of proof, to question is wrong, it is regarded
quiz.e: The linguistic challenge of a book that has remained unaltered for fourteen hundred years is open even today; people of this age too, if they wish, can investigate and see for themselves.

quiz.q: Someone says, the Prophet's ﷺ ability to bring the Qur’an is really his personal intellect and talent. What reply can be given with the ummi argument?
o: In reality there is no answer to this question
Literature like this coming without studying under a teacher is hard to explain by intellect
If one has talent, education is not needed at all
This may be true; talented people can really do everything
quiz.e: According to Surah al-‘Ankabut 48 he had not read any book before nor written; yet what even the best poets of Arabic could not do came out of his mouth.

quiz.q: If one has a tendency to hide one's own mistakes or weaknesses under others' pressure, what caution comes from the incident of al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah?
o: Hiding the truth under social pressure is natural and acceptable
Social standing is the most important thing
Always revealing the truth is a dangerous thing
Denying the truth creates inner conflict
quiz.e: Walid, though knowing the truth in his heart, denied it out of fear for social honour; the Qur’an itself brings out this self-deception as a warning.

quiz.q: Who bore witness, having seen the splitting of the moon with their own eyes?
o: Only Abu Bakr (RA)
Several Companions, including Anas and Ibn Mas‘ud
Only the disbelieving leaders of Makkah
Only members of the Prophet's ﷺ family
quiz.e: In Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim, Anas, Ibn Mas‘ud and Ibn ‘Abbas (RA) gave direct testimony of this event through several chains.

quiz.q: What happened after the Prophet's ﷺ supplication during the drought of Madinah?
o: The sky remained clear
A little cloud gathered but there was no rain, it is regarded
Rain came down at once from a cloudless sky
Only a cold wind began to blow
quiz.e: Though there was no cloud in the sky, right after the supplication a cloud rose and rain came, and for the next week the sun was not seen (Sahih al-Bukhari). On the next Friday, by another supplication, that rain was turned around the city.

quiz.q: How were ‘Ali's (RA) eye troubles healed on the eve of the Battle of Khaybar?
o: Slowly, after long treatment, it is regarded
By the treatment of another Companion
By themselves within a few days
In an instant by the Prophet's ﷺ saliva and supplication
quiz.e: When the Prophet ﷺ applied his own saliva to the inflamed eyes of ‘Ali (RA) and made supplication, they were healed in an instant; that very day the banner of Khaybar was placed in his hand (Sahih al-Bukhari, Sahih Muslim).

quiz.q: What is the lesson's explanation for the disbelievers not believing even after seeing the splitting of the moon?
o: There was in fact a shortage of signs
The door of the heart was already shut
The problem was really in their eyes
In the darkness of night they could not see well
quiz.e: The problem was not of eyes or proof, the problem was inside; when a prior decision is lodged in the heart, even the clearest proof can be disregarded.

quiz.q: Considering together the two events of bringing rain down and later stopping it, what is proven?
o: The weather changed by itself, it is regarded
The Companions exaggerated the incident
The effect of the same supplication worked in two opposite directions
It is a mere coincidence
quiz.e: Once bringing rain down from the sky, once turning that rain around the city; both opposite results happened with just a single supplication.

quiz.q: The category of proof into which the prophecy of Surah al-Rum falls, how is it different from a miracle like the splitting of the moon?
o: It was current only among poets
It is also a physical miracle seen with the eyes
It is never counted as proof of prophethood; so it is regarded
A prophecy given before the event, proved true afterward
quiz.e: Instead of an immediate event like the splitting of the moon, it is proof of advance knowledge, or news of the unseen, which came true years later.

quiz.q: Considering together the different kinds of proof described in this lesson (character, language, miracles seen with the eyes, scriptural testimony, prophecy), what is the main message?
o: Only one proof was really sufficient
The proofs are regarded as conflicting with one another
The claim to prophethood is supported by many kinds of proof
These are meaningful only to Muslims
quiz.e: Character, language, events seen with the eyes, scriptural testimony and prophecy together build a multi-layered, mutually supporting structure of proof.

quiz.q: When in a hard problem (financial crisis, illness) it seems hard to keep trust in supplication, what lesson from the rain miracle is useful?
o: Supplication is of no use, effort is enough, it is regarded
When one makes supplication the solution comes at once
Supplication should be made only in great calamities
Even without any sign, Allah can change things through supplication
quiz.e: Even with no sign at all, rain came by the Prophet's ﷺ supplication; this teaches us to make supplication with trust and patience, but the result depends on Allah's will.

quiz.q: In which aspect of this lesson does the habit of verifying the source before narrating an incident show most clearly?
o: Only the verses of the Qur’an were considered sufficient
No source of the incidents was mentioned, it is regarded
From each miracle having a hadith reference
All the incidents were narrated only by oral sources
quiz.e: Each miracle and incident carrying the specific hadith number of Sahih al-Bukhari and Sahih Muslim reflects the careful method of this lesson; before narrating any incident it is important to know the source.

porbos.title: The Testimony Written in the Earlier Books • How the Door of Prophethood Was Closed • The Beginning of Secret Da‘wah • A House That Was Opened • As Many as in Three Years • Final Word

blocks.0: The Testimony Written in the Earlier Books
blocks.1: The proof is not only in the present. Allah had kept proof in the past too; long before his coming.
blocks.3: Those who follow the Messenger, the unlettered Prophet; whom they find written about with them in the Torah and the Injil.{{1}}
blocks.4: They do not find. They find written. That is, it was already written beforehand.
blocks.5: ‘Isa (AS) even spoke the name itself with his own mouth.
blocks.7: And when ‘Isa ibn Maryam said, O Children of Israel! I am the messenger of Allah to you, confirming the Torah that came before me; and giving glad tidings of a Messenger who will come after me, whose name is Ahmad.{{1}}
blocks.8: That this testimony was not only on paper, there is a living proof.
blocks.10: ‘Abdullah ibn Salam, the greatest Jewish scholar of Madinah. The Book was in his memory, read since childhood. The signs were at his fingertips; how many times he had told his students, one day someone will come, check against this description.
blocks.11: That day suddenly there was an uproar in the city. People were running out of their homes, saying to one another, he has come, he has come. ‘Abdullah ran too. Pushing through the crowd, jostled again and again, he made his way to the very front.
blocks.12: He looked at the face only once.
blocks.13: Then he said, this is not the face of a liar. A lifetime of waiting, ended by just seeing a face; yet he did not stop there.
blocks.14: Because he is not a man to sit relying only on a face. The rigour he had learned page after page in the books, he applied here too. He verified by asking a few questions. Then he accepted Islam.
blocks.16: He asked, answer three questions; no one but a prophet knows these. The first question, what is the first sign of the Hour? The second question, what will the people of Paradise eat first in Paradise? The third question, a child sometimes resembles the father, sometimes the mother; what is the reason for this?
blocks.17: The Prophet {{1}} did not think even a moment. He answered one after another. The first sign, a fire that will drive people from the east to the west. The first food in Paradise, the extra lobe of a fish’s liver. And the child’s appearance depends on the course of the seed; if the father’s part goes first the child resembles the father, if the mother’s part goes first, the mother.{{2}}
blocks.18: All three questions answered without error; answers that cannot be given by rummaging through any book. ‘Abdullah ibn Salam could no longer stand there. He said, I bear witness that you are the Messenger of Allah.{{1}}
blocks.19: There are two paths of recognizing. One of the heart; one who recognizes at a single glance. The other of verification; one who becomes certain by asking question after question. He used both.
blocks.20: But recognizing and submitting are not the same thing.
blocks.21: Many of them recognized; yet did not bow their heads.
blocks.22: Knowing is not faith. Knowing and then bowing the head, that is faith.
blocks.23: It is the same in our homes.
blocks.24: We know that interest is haram.
blocks.25: We know that the prayer is being missed.
blocks.26: It is not for lack of knowing that we are stuck.
blocks.27: We are stuck at the place of not moving even after knowing.
blocks.28: How the Door of Prophethood Was Closed
blocks.29: A long caravan of prophets had come. Beginning from Adam (AS). One after another. Age after age. That caravan has come to him and stopped.
blocks.31: Muhammad is not the father of any of your men; but he is the Messenger of Allah and the last of the prophets.{{1}}
blocks.32: Khatam an-Nabiyyin. The seal of the prophets.
blocks.33: When the writing of a letter is finished, the mouth of the envelope is sealed. After the seal is put, nothing more enters that envelope. On the letter of prophethood the seal has been put. The Prophet {{1}} himself made the matter clear. He said, there is no prophet after me.{{2}}
blocks.34: After this, whoever stands up with a claim to prophethood, his claim will go in clash not with any scholar; but directly with this verse.
blocks.35: The False Claim of Musaylimah the Liar
blocks.36: An attempt to break this seal happened once in the lifetime of the Prophet {{1}} himself.
blocks.37: Musaylimah, leader of Yamamah, claimed to be a prophet. He sent two envoys to the Prophet {{1}} in Madinah, with a letter in hand. The letter was opened. At the very start was written, from Musaylimah, the messenger of Allah, to Muhammad, the messenger of Allah. Then was written, come, let half the earth be mine and half yours.
blocks.38: The whole assembly silent. Everyone’s eyes on the face of the Prophet {{1}}. The Prophet {{2}} asked the two envoys, do you bear witness that I am the messenger of Allah? They said, we bear witness that Musaylimah too is a messenger.
blocks.39: The face of the Prophet {{1}} turned stern. He said, if you were not envoys, I would have had your necks struck off.
blocks.40: Then he took the pen and wrote the reply himself. The earth belongs to Allah; He makes whom He wills of His servants inherit it. And the final outcome is for the God-fearing alone.{{1}}
blocks.41: Musaylimah still did not give up the claim. After the passing of the Prophet {{1}}, in the caliphate of Abu Bakr (RA), on the plain of Yamamah his army was defeated; he himself was killed in that battle. The claim of false prophethood stopped there forever.
blocks.42: Such a claim arose in the very lifetime of the Prophet {{1}}, and was also extinguished. This itself shows that the seal was intact that day, and is intact today.
blocks.44: In the nineteenth century Mirza Ghulam Ahmad Qadiani raised exactly this same claim anew. The scholars of the Ummah, in consensus, have declared him and his followers outside the bounds of Islam. Holding to this belief is part of the faith of every Muslim. Because breaking the seal does not mean touching some minor issue; it is swinging an axe at the greatest pillar of the religion.
blocks.45: Precisely because the door is closed, this matter is useful even today.
blocks.46: Even today some people claim that special news comes to them.
blocks.47: Someone says I received a command in a dream. Someone says inspiration descends upon me.
blocks.48: Ordinary people then fall into confusion.
blocks.49: Yet the measuring-rod is very short.
blocks.50: The door of prophethood is closed.
blocks.51: Someone’s dream can come true; but no new word of the religion stands on the basis of a dream.
blocks.52: If anyone says a new command has come to me, however great a saint he pretends to be, that statement is false.
blocks.54: Right after the claim of prophethood the da‘wah did not begin openly; the first three years passed in secret.
blocks.56: The first to believe was Khadijah (RA); the first among women. Then ‘Ali ibn Abi Talib (RA); his age then eight or ten years, the youngest in age. Then Zayd ibn Harithah (RA); the first among freed slaves. And the first among free men Abu Bakr (RA); the closest friend of the Prophet {{1}}, who believed at a single call.{{2}}
blocks.58: Makkah was still sunk in idol worship; this new religion there was negligible in number, helpless in strength. So the da‘wah went on in private, house to house, to trustworthy people. Before going to anyone it was first judged, will this man be able to bear it?
blocks.59: After believing himself, Abu Bakr (RA) began to invite his close friends; men like ‘Uthman, Talhah, Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas, Zubayr ibn al-‘Awwam (RA) came to Islam in this way.{{1}}
blocks.60: The Man Who Never Paused for a Moment
blocks.61: What concerns Abu Bakr (RA) is worth saying separately.
blocks.62: The Prophet {{1}} later said, whomever I invited to Islam, I saw in him some hesitation; a stopping short, a thinking over, an asking for time.
blocks.64: On hearing, he had said, yes.{{1}}
blocks.65: He had known the man for forty years. There was nothing left to verify.
blocks.66: That Boy in the Corner of the House
blocks.67: ‘Ali (RA) then lived in the house of the Prophet {{1}} itself. Age eight or ten.
blocks.68: One day entering the house he saw the Prophet {{1}} and Khadijah (RA) standing doing something.
blocks.70: Hearing the answer the boy said, let me think a little.
blocks.71: He thought all night. In the morning he came and believed.{{1}}
blocks.73: Secret da‘wah needed a fixed address; a place where the believers could gather safely, hear the Qur’an from the mouth of the Prophet {{1}}, learn the prayer. That place was the house of al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam at the foot of the hill of Safa.
blocks.74: Arqam was young, and by tribe of Banu Makhzum; the tribe that was foremost in openly opposing the Prophet {{1}}. So no one suspected that the followers of the Prophet {{2}} sit in this house.
blocks.75: In this very house the Prophet {{1}} would recite the Qur’an to the new believers, explain the meaning of the verses, teach ablution and prayer hands-on, give instruction in keeping the heart clean. When anyone new came to Islam he was secretly brought right here.
blocks.76: This is the first madrasa of Islam; the first classroom. One teacher, a countable few students, and a closed door.
blocks.77: In these three years of secret da‘wah the group did not grow much. Later, when in the early days of open da‘wah ‘Umar ibn al-Khattab (RA) accepted Islam, even then the number of believers in this very Dar al-Arqam was about forty.{{1}}
blocks.78: What the Prayer Was Like Then
blocks.79: A question stands here. Which prayer did they pray then!
blocks.80: The five daily prayers had not yet become obligatory. That would come much later, on the night of the Mi‘raj.
blocks.81: But the prayer was there from the very beginning.
blocks.82: Jibril (AS) came and taught the Prophet {{1}} ablution. Then the prayer.{{2}}
blocks.83: Two rak‘ahs in the morning, two rak‘ahs in the evening.
blocks.84: ‘A’ishah (RA) says, when the prayer became obligatory it was two rak‘ahs each; later the prayer of the resident was increased, and the prayer of the traveller remained as before.{{1}}
blocks.85: And in the very surah of the first revelation it has come, someone is forbidding a servant whom he sees praying.{{1}}
blocks.86: The prayer had begun right then. The obstruction had begun right then too.
blocks.88: Praying secretly, one day a few Companions were caught.
blocks.89: A valley outside Makkah. Standing behind the rocks they were praying.
blocks.90: A group of polytheists saw them. They came close and began to jeer. Then they raised their hands.
blocks.91: Sa‘d ibn Abi Waqqas (RA), finding a camel bone at hand, struck it on a man’s head. Blood flowed.{{1}}
blocks.92: The first blood shed on the path of Islam.
blocks.93: The prayer then had to be prayed in hiding. And even that hidden prayer they could not bear.
blocks.94: The three years of the secret phase passed in just this way. A small group, growing quietly; that silence before the storm rises.
blocks.96: Dar al-Arqam once more. An ordinary house at the foot of the hill of Safa. The owner’s name al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam. Age then sixteen or seventeen.
blocks.97: This house became the first madrasa of Islam. Here the Qur’an was taught. The prayer was taught. And that thing was taught which is not had by reading books; the cleansing of the heart.{{1}}
blocks.98: A secret assembly is sitting in the boy’s house. If Quraysh found out, the house itself would not remain. Yet he opened the door.
blocks.99: And he was no orator. No scholar. No commander. He had only given a house. And the name of that house has endured for fourteen hundred years.
blocks.100: Our own house is like this too. In our house there is a sitting room. There is a dining room. The best place in front of the television is reserved. And which place is reserved for the religion!
blocks.101: The question is not of building a mosque. The question is of one evening in the week. The people of the house sit together and read the Qur’an for ten minutes. Or listen to one story of the Seerah. That much, no more.
blocks.102: Arqam (RA) gave the house at the risk of his life. We have no risk. Only the time has to be given.
blocks.103: And one more thing. In a house where the religion is not spoken of, other things are spoken of. The place is never empty.
blocks.104: So start one thing from today. Fix one day in the week. Sit with everyone in the house for ten minutes. Ten minutes is enough. Dar al-Arqam too began with an ordinary house.
blocks.105: As Many as in Three Years
blocks.106: The calculation is this. Three years the da‘wah went on. Day after day, house to house, one by one. And how many accepted Islam in these three years! Forty or fifty.
blocks.107: If it were today, what would we say! We would say, the method is not working. We would say, people are not listening. We would say, this will not do; another path must be taken.
blocks.108: And the biggest point. The one giving the da‘wah is the Messenger of Allah. No one can speak better than him. Yet in three years, forty people.
blocks.109: Giving results is not our job. Our job is to convey. And it is mixing up these two that makes people give up.
blocks.110: What do we do today! I told my son about prayer for two days. He did not listen. On the third day I stopped telling him. I said in my heart, nothing will come of him.
blocks.111: Three days. And he gave three years. Even then he did not stop; rather from there he came down into the open.
blocks.112: And that forty. The number is small. But by the hands of these forty the whole of Arabia changed afterwards. Allah did not look at numbers; He made men. And making men takes time.
blocks.113: Take up one task. The one you have given up on after telling and telling, tell him once more this week. Not with a scolding. Anew, as if for the first time.
blocks.115: In today’s lesson we saw the proofs behind a claim.
blocks.116: Forty years of spotless character, which had borne witness long before the claim. A miracle, which still lies open before every person today. Signs seen with the eyes like the moon splitting in two. Testimony written in the earlier Books, which changed a Jewish scholar in an instant. And last of all, the declaration that the door of prophethood is closed forever.
blocks.117: One claim, surrounded by so many kinds of proof; this has not happened in the case of any other prophet.
blocks.118: Al-Walid ibn al-Mughirah knew the truth in his heart, yet out of fear of his people denied it with his mouth. ‘Utbah ibn Rabi‘ah trembled merely on hearing a recitation. ‘Abdullah ibn Salam, seeing just a face, said, this is not the face of a liar. Three men, three kinds of reaction; but the inner testimony of all three met at one place.
blocks.119: The phase of that three years’ secret da‘wah has passed too. In the next lesson we will see how Makkah reacted after the open proclamation on the hill of Safa, and by which road the next step of the da‘wah rolled on.
blocks.121: On that day Khadijah (RA) did not ask for proof. Relying on a character known for forty years she stood by his side.
blocks.122: Today I will ask myself one question, who in my house is broken today, and have I stood by his side?
blocks.123: Today instead of advising him I will remind him of one of his good deeds, which from today I will not give up.

quiz.q: What was the subject of the three questions ‘Abdullah ibn Salam (RA) asked the Prophet ﷺ?
o: The signs of the Hour, the food of Paradise and the resemblance of a child
The detailed rules and conditions of prayer, fasting, zakat and Hajj
The ethics of war and running a state
The rules and customs of his own lineage and tribe
quiz.e: He tested by asking three questions that no one but a prophet knows; on the flawless answers of the Prophet ﷺ he accepted Islam (Sahih al-Bukhari hadith no. 3329).

quiz.q: From the process of ‘Abdullah ibn Salam’s acceptance of Islam, what method of decision-making emerges?
o: Decisions should be made on logical proof alone
He became certain just by seeing the face and accepted Islam at once
One should rely only on others’ opinions
Deciding by combining both the feeling of the heart and verification
quiz.e: First he understood with the heart on seeing the face, then verified by asking hard questions; only by using both paths did he reach the final decision.

quiz.q: Someone gives an opinion quickly without knowing the answer to a question for sure. What can be learned here from ‘Abdullah ibn Salam’s method of verification?
o: A decision should be made by taking others’ opinions
The first feeling is enough; there is no need for separate verification
However strong the first impression, it is good to ask and be sure
Making quick decisions is the wise thing
quiz.e: He could have been certain just on seeing the face, yet he verified by asking hard questions; this habit of verifying without haste is the basis of responsible decision.

quiz.q: What is the Prophet ﷺ called in verse 40 of Surah al-Ahzab?
o: The very first messenger
The last of the prophets
One of equal rank to all the prophets
A prophet of Arabia only
quiz.e: The verse says he is the Messenger of Allah and the last of the prophets (Khatam an-Nabiyyin); after him the door of prophethood is closed forever.

quiz.q: In what respect were Musaylimah al-Kadhdhab and Mirza Ghulam Ahmad Qadiani alike?
o: Both raised their claims in the same age
Both later withdrew their claims
Both raised claims at different times, and the Ummah rejected them
The Ummah rejected only one, not the other; so it is regarded
quiz.e: Though separated in time (one in the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, the other in the nineteenth century), the nature of both claims is the same, and the Ummah’s reaction is equally firm.

quiz.q: What is the argument for comparing the finality of prophethood to the seal of a letter?
o: After the seal is put nothing enters the envelope; so with prophethood, an end
The custom of letter-writing was brand new then
The Companions themselves used this simile, it is regarded
Prophethood was literally a letter
quiz.e: The simile is conceptual; just as inserting anything new in an envelope after the seal is meaningless, so a claim of a new prophethood after the Prophet ﷺ is baseless.

quiz.q: Why does the lesson call the Ummah’s position on the Qadiani fitnah ‘part of faith’?
o: The Qadianis spoke a different language
Denying the finality of prophethood strikes the very foundation of the religion
It is merely a political decision; so it is regarded
It was only a regional problem
quiz.e: The finality of prophethood is not some minor issue; it is one of the greatest pillars of the religion, so denying it clashes directly with faith.

quiz.q: If someone claims a new prophethood in today’s age, what should a Muslim’s position be, according to the lesson?
o: The claim should be examined to see whether he is truly a prophet
Decide according to the local custom, it is regarded
Stay silent and avoid deciding
Reject it outright, since the door of prophethood is closed forever
quiz.e: According to Surah al-Ahzab 40 and several sahih hadiths, after the Prophet ﷺ there is no question of considering any claim of new prophethood; it is rejected outright.

quiz.q: What does the incident of Musaylimah teach about recognizing false claimants or deceivers in society?
o: A false claim does not last in the end
A false claim cannot be refuted by proof
All claimants should be believed
Avoiding false claimants is the only solution
quiz.e: Though Musaylimah’s claim seemed strong in the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ, in the end it was destroyed; against truth, falsehood is not long-lasting.

quiz.q: After the claim of prophethood, for how long did the da‘wah first go on in secret?
o: One year
Ten years
Seven years
Three years
quiz.e: After the claim of prophethood, for the first three years the da‘wah went on in secret, in private; after that came the open proclamation on the hill of Safa.

quiz.q: Woman, youth, freed slave and free man; who were the very first to accept Islam in these four categories?
o: Khadijah, ‘Ali, Zayd, Abu Bakr
‘A’ishah, ‘Umar, Bilal, ‘Uthman
Hafsah, Husayn, Salman, Talhah
Fatimah, Hasan, ‘Ammar, Sa‘d
quiz.e: Among women Khadijah, among youths ‘Ali, among freed slaves Zayd, and among free men Abu Bakr (RA) were the very first to believe.

quiz.q: Which house was the centre of instruction and gathering of the believers during the secret da‘wah?
o: The house of Abu Bakr, it is regarded
The house of al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam
The house of Khadijah
The house of ‘Ali
quiz.e: In the house of al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam at the foot of the hill of Safa the Prophet ﷺ secretly taught the Qur’an, and taught prayer and tazkiyah; this is Dar al-Arqam.

quiz.q: Why was the secret da‘wah of three years needed?
o: The Prophet ﷺ was not yet ready to give da‘wah
Quraysh did not yet know the matter, so it was kept secret from all; so it is regarded
There was a specific command in Islam to keep it secret
The new religion was negligible in number then, and had no strength to bear it if it came into the open
quiz.e: In the idol-worshipping society of Makkah the new group was still weak in number and strength; the condition to bear it had not yet formed if it came into the open.

quiz.q: Why is Dar al-Arqam called the first madrasa of Islam?
o: The Prophet ﷺ regularly gave instruction there in the Qur’an, prayer and purification of the heart
One of the largest libraries and scriptoriums of that age was built there
Only the Arabic language was taught there
Children of all tribes studied there
quiz.e: One teacher, a handful of students and a closed door; here the Prophet ﷺ explained the Qur’an to the believers, taught ablution and prayer hands-on, and gave instruction in keeping the heart clean.

quiz.q: About how old was al-Arqam ibn Abi al-Arqam (RA), the owner of Dar al-Arqam, then?
o: Sixteen or seventeen
Twenty-five or twenty-six
Close to forty
Over fifty
quiz.e: His ordinary house at the foot of the hill of Safa became the first madrasa of Islam. There is variation of narration about his age.

quiz.q: On the basis of the words ‘In a house where the religion is not spoken of, other things are spoken of’, what act is given in the lesson?
o: Making a separate worship room in the house
Sitting with everyone one day a week for ten minutes
Building a large collection of books in the house; so it is regarded
Holding a long gathering daily with everyone
quiz.e: Dar al-Arqam too began with an ordinary house; the place is never empty.

quiz.q: From the small number of people accepting Islam in the three years of secret da‘wah, what point does the lesson draw?
o: The method of da‘wah of that age was not effective enough; so it is regarded
Giving da‘wah in secret was actually wrong
Giving results is not our job, conveying is our job
If the number is small, that da‘wah should be abandoned
quiz.e: The number was small, but by the hands of these forty the whole of Arabia changed afterwards.

quiz.q: When telling someone again and again does not work, what is to be done according to the chapter on Dar al-Arqam and secret da‘wah?
o: Change the method and speak in harsh words
Wait in complete silence for some days
Arrange for someone else to tell it
Tell again anew, as if for the first time
quiz.e: We give up in three days; he gave three years, and even then he did not stop.
